policy_prompt_for_memory.name: bin_center
policy_prompt_for_memory.description: At initialization, the hand was high above an unobstructed bin and both calibrated views showed its opening. The policy repeatedly wrote unknown while the annotation held a reconstructed center. This is a PREDICTABILITY failure in applying the acceptance criterion, not a missing historical fact. Clarify that unknown is reserved for genuinely underconstrained geometry, not ordinary pixel-estimation uncertainty. In these clear two-view situations, match the inner opening's corners in cyclic order, triangulate corresponding corners using the two camera calibrations, and check that they form a horizontal rectangle whose reprojections agree with the visible inner rim. Compute the xy center from its opposing corners. When the plausible corner fits constrain the center within 1 cm, write that center immediately; an example is [0.024, -0.095]. Exact pixel agreement is not required. Do not match an outer-rim corner to an inner-rim corner. Retain the existing initialization, preservation, correction, and displacement rules otherwise.

proposal.policy_prompt_for_action: At initial cube approaches, small top faces were localized with enough bias to put the chosen waypoint more than 1 cm from the recorded target. Similar numerical localization error occurred on an approach to the stop button after all quotas were complete. These are SUFFICIENCY failures of geometric estimation, not evidence that another historical field is needed. Strengthen the existing localization procedure: for a cube, identify the four top-face corners rather than the centroid of the whole colored patch, intersect their calibrated rays with z approximately 0.04, and fit a square in world coordinates. Use the fitted square's center for xy and its world-space edges for yaw. When both views show the face, check the same fitted square against both views, rejecting a fit biased toward a visible side face. This applies especially to the small cube faces in the initial high wrist view. For the button, fit the gray circular top in its approximately z=0.02 plane and verify the resulting center against the available second view; do not use the square base or a rounded whole-object centroid. Keep the existing approach heights, gripper commands, and approach-to-descent target continuity. For initial bin localization, explicitly use the memory instruction's two-view corner-fit acceptance test: normal estimation uncertainty does not justify a visibility-recovery motion when the center is already constrained within 1 cm. Do not change deposit counting, release, retreat, or completion behavior.
proposal.refused: The reports correctly expose an unresolved choice among multiple accessible eligible cubes, both initially and after retreats. However, they do not establish a common selection rule that reproduces the recorded choices. Suggested rules such as robot-nearest conflict with the supplied world coordinates and with other selections: the robot is on the negative-x side, so a foreground cube with larger x is not generally the robot-nearest cube. Other reports request different image extrema or a middle foreground cube without giving a common criterion. The goal specifies color quotas, not cube identity or order, and no earlier observable selection establishes these later targets. I therefore do not pass on episode-specific coordinates, image-pixel targets, a count-indexed target schedule, or an invented nearest/rightmost priority as a general correction. The selection SUFFICIENCY problem remains unresolved by the supplied evidence; reproducing those exact choices requires a supported selection convention rather than additional historical memory. Likewise, requests for particular yaw representatives among equivalent square-edge grasps do not establish a consistent convention, and the stated sufficiency comparison concerns position and gripper state, not those equivalent orientations. The existing instruction already permits unrestricted feasible edge-aligned yaw. The bin annotation itself needs no change: it already requires reconstruction from geometry available at that cycle and forbids hindsight or action-destination substitution; only the policy's acceptance guidance needs clarification. Keep deposited_green conditionally defined, not merged or deleted: none of the supplied goals requests green, so the existing rule omits it and its lack of reads is expected. It carries no value in these episodes; when green is requested, its independent quota cannot be represented by a blue or red count. The reports with no identified missing information do not justify new state or episode-specific waypoint corrections.

fields.name: deposited_blue
fields.description: Include only when blue is requested. Initialize to 0 when memory is empty; otherwise carry forward. Increment once when this cycle's incoming motion shows either a blue cube carried over the bin followed by an empty open hand, or a blue cube separating or falling directly below the fingers over the opening followed by an empty open hand. The sampled frames need not show the finger-opening transition itself. Require evidence of a new release from this hand over the bin; a stationary tabletop cube below the hand or an unrelated falling cube is not release evidence. Identify color from the carried or newly released cube, not remaining tabletop objects. Alternatively, when incoming held_color is blue, count a newly established transition to an empty open hand over the bin in the executed incoming release motion, with no evidence of loss elsewhere, even if all sampled frames omit the cube. Use incoming held_color before clearing it. This is an alternative evidence test for the same release, not an additional increment; an already empty hand or a no-step motion does not qualify. Count even if the resting cube is hidden and even if the motion includes retreat. Never increment for the command about to be issued, an already empty hand, a grasp, a closed transfer, retreat without a new release, or a motion executing no steps. Preserve through button pressing. e.g. 2
fields.annotation: Include only when blue is requested. Cumulative number of blue cubes released from the gripper into the bin during execution, initially 0. Increment once at the first act cycle whose incoming motion contains the completed blue release over the opening, including release followed by retreat. Identify color before release; count even when the deposited cube becomes hidden. Do not increment when merely choosing the opening command, for grasps or closed transfers, or for later views of a completed release. Preserve otherwise, including through button pressing. e.g. 2

fields.name: held_color
fields.description: Values are none, blue, green, or red. Initialize to none. Set to the visibly grasped cube's color when current views and finger opening establish a successful grasp. Retain through closed lifting and transfer, including temporary visual occlusion while possession remains supported. When the hand becomes empty, evaluate deposit updates using incoming held_color before writing none. Clear without counting when loss occurs away from the bin. Do not set from a future grasp target or clear merely because an opening command is about to be issued. e.g. red
fields.annotation: Color of the cube currently held: none, blue, green, or red. Initially none. Set to the cube's color at the first cycle showing a successful grasp. Retain through closed lifting and transfer, including temporary occlusion while possession remains supported. Clear to none at the first cycle showing the hand empty after release or loss. Record observed possession, not a selected grasp target or an opening command about to execute. Deposit-count annotations retain their existing completed-release timing. e.g. red

fields.name: bin_center
fields.description: World xy center of the bin's inner opening, written as [x, y] in metres, or unknown. Initialize to unknown. When this cycle's calibrated views reliably constrain the center using the action instruction's geometric reconstruction and reprojection checks, write that center immediately. Unknown is reserved for genuinely underconstrained geometry, not ordinary pixel-estimation uncertainty. When both views clearly show the opening, identify corresponding inner-rim corners in consistent cyclic order, triangulate them using the respective camera calibrations, and fit a horizontal rectangle. Check its reprojections against the visible inner rim and compute its world xy center from opposing corners. Never match an outer-rim corner to an inner-rim corner. Accept the fit when plausible corner fits constrain the center within 0.01 m in each world coordinate; exact pixel agreement is not required. This two-view test does not exclude the action instruction's geometrically constrained single-view reconstruction. Otherwise retain the incoming value through occlusion, transfers, releases, and retreats. Update an established value only when reliable current geometry supports a correction or establishes bin displacement. If displacement is established but the new center cannot be reconstructed, write unknown. A cropped view or partial occlusion alone does not invalidate the retained center. Do not overwrite it with the centroid of a visible dark fragment, an occluding silhouette, measured TCP position, or the destination of an action being selected. e.g. [-0.02, -0.09]
fields.annotation: World xy center of the bin's inner opening, written as [x, y] in metres, or unknown. Initially unknown. Set at the first cycle whose available calibrated views reliably constrain the center using geometric reconstruction and reprojection checks. Retain through occlusion, transfers, releases, and retreats. Revise only when reliable current geometry establishes a correction or an observed displacement of the bin. If displacement is established but the new center cannot be reconstructed, write unknown. Use only geometry available by this cycle; do not backfill from later views or substitute recorded action destinations for visual reconstruction. e.g. [-0.02, -0.09]

texts.action:
Read a separate quota for each requested color from the goal each cycle. For each color, compute its completed count from its incoming deposited_<color> memory plus only that color's newly completed release in the current incoming motion, exactly once, using the memory instruction's sparse-frame evidence test. A carried cube followed by an empty open hand, or a cube visibly separating or falling from the fingers over the opening followed by an empty open hand, can establish the release without a sampled finger-opening transition. Also apply the memory instruction's incoming-held_color test when the released cube is absent from all incoming samples. Evaluate that test before clearing held_color, and compute completion from the resulting per-color counts, not from outgoing held_color. Multiple evidence tests for one release still produce only one increment. Do not add the release again to an already updated count. A color is eligible only while its own quota remains outstanding. Completion requires every requested color's quota to be satisfied. Start with an open hand and zero deposits for each requested color. Infer object positions from calibrated front and wrist views rather than treating image coordinates as world coordinates. Cubes are approximately 4 cm wide: identify their four top-face corners, intersect the calibrated corner rays with the plane at approximately z=0.04, and fit a square in world coordinates. Use the fitted square's center for approach xy and the z=0.02 grasp, and its world-space edges for feasible edge-aligned yaw. When both views show the face, check the same fitted square against both views. Apply this procedure also to small faces in a high wrist view. Use the top face, not the whole colored patch or visible silhouette; reject fits biased toward a visible side face. Preserve the existing approached-cube identity and orientation through descent and lift. For the bin center, use a reliable current reconstruction when available; otherwise use incoming bin_center unless current observations establish that the bin moved. Partial occlusion or cropping alone does not invalidate a retained center. To obtain or reliably correct the center, reconstruct the bin's rectangular inner opening using the available calibrated current views. For each image point [u,v,1], form a world ray with camera center C=-R^T t and direction d=R^T K^-1[u,v,1], using that camera's current calibration. Prefer reliable two-view correspondences between actual inner-rim corners or edge intersections: triangulate them and fit their common horizontal plane. For a clearly visible opening, match inner-rim corners in consistent cyclic order and apply the bin_center memory instruction's horizontal-rectangle fit and reprojection acceptance test. Do not match inner-rim corners to outer-rim corners. Ordinary pixel-estimation uncertainty does not justify unknown or a visibility-recovery motion when plausible fits already constrain the center within 0.01 m in each world coordinate; exact pixel agreement is not required. When such correspondences are unavailable, accept a single-view reconstruction if visible geometry constrains it. Identify actual table-contact base corners and their corresponding vertical wall edges; intersect base-corner rays with z=0, then fit corresponding upper corners along the world-vertical lines through those base corners to determine the rim plane. Back-project inner-rim edge points into that plane and fit the rectangular opening. Use visible opposing edges and reconstruct obscured portions only where the fitted geometry constrains them. Compute the world center from opposing corners or edge midlines, and verify reprojection against all available visible rim segments, including partial wrist edges. Do not shift the center toward a visible side wall, use the centroid of an exposed dark fragment, average image centroids across cameras, treat occluding silhouettes as rim correspondences, or intersect the opening center with the tabletop. A cropped wrist view or partial opening occlusion alone does not require visibility recovery. Use the purposeful visibility-recovery motion below only when neither current geometry nor a valid retained bin_center supplies a reliable center; do not invent a numeric rim height. Use the center selected by this current-reconstruction-or-memory rule consistently for closed transfer and separate release at z=0.20 and for retreat at [bin_x-0.10,bin_y,0.20]. Locate the button by its gray circular top on a light square base. Fit the circular top in its world plane at approximately z=0.02 using calibrated rays from its visible boundary, and verify the fitted circle's reprojection against the other current view when available. Use the fitted world xy center for approach, empty-gripper closing, and press; do not use the square base or a rounded whole-object centroid. Re-estimate cube and button positions from current views; scene objects can appear during execution. For the bin, apply the current-reconstruction-or-memory rule rather than requiring fresh localization. Robot right is negative world y.

When any color quota remains outstanding and the hand is empty away from the bin's release position, select a visible, accessible tabletop cube of an eligible color. Prefer a clear grasp and maintain the selection when the hand is already aligned above an eligible cube; do not switch cubes or colors simply because new cubes appear. Never select another cube of a color whose quota is already satisfied. Approach its center at z=0.15 with the gripper open, roll=-3.1416, pitch=0, and a feasible yaw aligned with a cube edge. Do not constrain yaw to [-0.7854,0.7854]. Re-estimate edge alignment for each newly selected cube rather than carrying over the previous cube's yaw, and preserve the selected orientation through descent and lift. When already above an eligible cube near z=0.15, identify the approached cube by projecting [current_tcp_x,current_tcp_y,0.04] into the current wrist image with its calibration. Identify the eligible top face nearest that projection, cross-checking world-space proximity and the incoming approach frames. Neither the wrist image center nor the largest visible cube is the alignment reference. Refine that same cube's top-face center at approximately z=0.04, then descend at its world xy to z=0.02 and close, preserving the approached cube's edge-aligned orientation. Do not switch to another prominent cube or descend at an inaccurate measured approach xy.

When a cube is grasped at table height, lift vertically to z=0.15, retaining its grasp orientation and keeping the gripper closed. A cube between the fingers and finger positions around 0.018 m support a successful grasp. Once lifted, move to the world xy center of the bin opening supplied by the current-reconstruction-or-memory rule at z=0.20, keeping the cube closed in the gripper and preserving the measured grasp orientation. After the closed-hand transfer reaches approximately z=0.20 above the bin, use that same rule to obtain the opening center and command open at [bin_x, bin_y, 0.20], correcting any residual lateral error in that waypoint. The target is the opening center, not the measured TCP xy. Opening remains a separate operation from the closed-hand transfer. Correct both lateral coordinates before testing whether the centered target would produce no motion; add a 0.003 m vertical displacement only in that case.

When the hand is empty and open at the bin after a release, including a release established using incoming held_color without a sampled separation, retreat toward the robot: target [bin_x-0.10, bin_y, 0.20], preserving orientation and keeping open. Compute this offset from the bin center supplied by the current-reconstruction-or-memory rule, never from measured TCP xy. Perform this retreat even after the final requested cube. If the incoming motion already included this retreat and the hand is at that offset, do not repeat it. Retreat clears the opening and gives the dropped cube time to fall; no separate arbitrary wait is needed.

When every requested color's quota is satisfied and the final release retreat is finished, ignore all remaining cubes. Approach the button center at z=0.15, roll=-3.1416, pitch=0, yaw=0, with the gripper open. When already aligned above the button with open fingers, re-localize the gray circular button-top center using the calibrated circle fit in the approximately z=0.02 plane and its available second-view reprojection check. Use the circular top, not the surrounding square base. Command [button_x,button_y,0.15,-3.1416,0,0] and close the empty gripper. Correct the target before testing the nonzero-motion requirement; add a 0.003 m vertical displacement only if the corrected target would otherwise produce no motion. When aligned above the button with closed fingers, descend to [button_x, button_y, 0.0075] with the gripper closed. If the current motion shows this descent reaching button contact, retract to [button_x, button_y, 0.15] with the gripper still closed. Contact can leave the measured TCP near z=0.0245 rather than the commanded depth; recognize the visible contact and retract instead of repeatedly demanding a deeper press.

For an unanticipated or ambiguous situation, use the visible hand contents, finger opening, height, and object alignment to recover the applicable rule. Never increase the deposit count without an observed release. If a grasp fails, reopen with a small nonzero upward motion and re-approach a visible requested-color cube. If any color quota remains outstanding but no suitable cube of an eligible color is currently available, wait 16 control steps specifically to observe newly arriving cubes, then reassess. If occlusion leaves an object needed for localization genuinely underconstrained after using the available calibrated views and visible geometry, and for the bin no valid retained bin_center supplies its center, move upward to a clear viewing height while retaining any held cube, then re-localize. Do not make this recovery motion merely because the wrist view crops the object or part of it is hidden. Never press the stop button before every requested color's quota is satisfied and the final release retreat is complete.

applied.refused: No episode-specific coordinates, image-pixel targets, count-indexed target schedule, fixed color priority, or nearest/rightmost cube ranking is added. Across rounds, the proposed rankings conflict and no supported general selection convention has been established; additional memory cannot predict arbitrary future recorded choices. No yaw representative convention or yaw-history field is added. No cube or button position memory is justified by current-view estimation errors. The bin_center annotation remains unchanged: its observed-geometry timing and prohibition on hindsight remain valid. The new acceptance guidance preserves both the single-view fallback and retained-center use established in earlier rounds; it does not restore mandatory two-camera reconstruction. Deposit counts, including conditionally present deposited_green, and held_color remain unchanged.
